'''Yuri Nikolayevich Babayev''' ({{langx|ru|Юрий Николаевич Бабаев}}; 21 May 1928 – 6 October 1986), {{small|[[Candidate of Sciences|k.N]]}}, was a Soviet [[Physics|physicist]] who spent a long career in the former [[Soviet atomic bomb project|Soviet program]] of [[nuclear weapons]], and known as one of the principles who designed the [[Tsar Bomba]], the largest-ever nuclear weapon.

==Early life==
He was born in [[Moscow]]. His family was evacuated during the battles of the [[Eastern Front (World War II)]], first to [[Chelyabinsk]] then to Leninabad (now [[Khujand]]). He did well at school despite the hardships.<ref name="Rosatom">{{cite web|url=http://www.biblioatom.ru/founders/babaev_yuriy_nikolaevich/|title=Бабаев Юрий Николаевич)(1928—1986)|website=www.biblioatom.ru|access-date=24 October 2018|archive-date=29 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629060453/http://www.biblioatom.ru/founders/babaev_yuriy_nikolaevich/|url-status=live}}</ref>

He graduated with honours from the faculty of Physics of [[Moscow State University]] in 1950. He entered the Soviet weapons programme as one of its youngest scientists, a senior laboratory assistant in [[Andrei Sakharov]]'s group at Arzamas-16 (also known as KB-11), now known as [[All-Russian Scientific Research Institute of Experimental Physics]] (VNIIEF), in [[Sarov]], [[Nizhny Novgorod]] region. In 1953, he received the [[USSR State Prize|Stalin Prize]] for his part in the work to develop the Soviet union's first [[thermonuclear weapon]], the [[RDS-6]] which was detonated in 1953; this was the first of several state awards for his work advancing nuclear weapons. With fellow physicist [[Yuri Trutnev (scientist)|Yuri Trutnev]], he proposed a new design in 1955 for a two-stage thermonuclear device with much-improved features, followed by theoretical development and finally completion in 1958. He frequently took part in testing weapons he had helped to develop. He received his Ph.D. in nuclear engineering in 1960. In 1962, he became a doctor of technical sciences and senior research worker. In 1964 he was promoted to head of his department and deputy head of VNIIEF.

His work also encompassed development of low-radiation-yield nuclear charges for civilian purposes – for example to make reservoirs – and nuclear-pumped lasers. He was also interested in the effects of radiation on humans and the environment. Many scientists were trained under his direction as Chair of the Academic Council at KB-11. He was elected to the [[Russian Academy of Sciences|Soviet Academy of Sciences]] in November 1968.<ref name="Rosatom"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1986/10/29/obituaries/yuri-n-babayev-dies-noted-soviet-physicist.html|work=New York Times|title=Yuri N. Babayev dies- noted Soviet physicist|location=New York|date=29 October 1986|access-date=4 October 2018|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|archive-date=25 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181025071000/https://www.nytimes.com/1986/10/29/obituaries/yuri-n-babayev-dies-noted-soviet-physicist.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=American and Soviet H-bomb development programmes: historical background|journal=Uspekhi Fizicheskikh Nauk, Russian Academy of Sciences|last=Goncharov|first=G.A.|volume=39|issue=10|pages=1033–1044|year=1996|doi=10.1070/PU1996v039n10ABEH000174|s2cid=250861572 }}</ref>

He was buried at [[Kuntsevo Cemetery]] in Moscow.<ref name="Rosatom"/>

==Awards==
* 1953: [[USSR State Prize|Stalin Prize]].
* 1956 & 1962: [[Order of the Red Banner of Labour]].
* 1959: [[Lenin Prize]].
* 1962: [[Hero of Socialist Labour]] & [[Order of Lenin]].
* 1975: [[Medal "For Labour Valour"]].
* 2000: (posthumously) [[State Prize of the Russian Federation]].
